![Agile vs Scrum: Understanding the Dynamics of Modern Project ...](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081545-2633-0066-0000-40861af1e003:4)
`Agile is a broad project management philosophy, while Scrum is a specific, structured framework used to put Agile principles into practice`.[[1]](https://projectmanagementacademy.net/resources/blog/agile-vs-scrum-what-you-need-to-know/)[[2]](https://business.adobe.com/blog/basics/agile-vs-scrum-project-management)

### What is Agile?

- **Definition:** A mindset and set of values centered on flexibility, continuous iteration, and customer collaboration.
- **Core Principles:** Rooted in the Agile Manifesto , prioritizing individuals, working solutions, and responding to change over strict processes.
- **Flexibility:** Does not mandate specific rules, mandatory meetings, or predefined roles.
- **Alternatives:** Can be implemented through various frameworks like Scrum or Kanban.[[1]](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/scrum/agile-vs-scrum)[[2]](https://miro.com/agile/scrum-vs-agile-methodology/)[[3]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/agile-vs-scrum)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bqi0EOlAmtU&t=13)[[5]](https://projectmanagementacademy.net/resources/blog/agile-vs-scrum-what-you-need-to-know/)[[6]](https://www.agilesherpas.com/blog/agile-vs-scrum)

### What is Scrum?

- **Definition:** A prescriptive framework designed to execute Agile values through defined cycles.
- **Structure:** Organizes work into fixed-length **Sprints** (usually 1 to 4 weeks long).
- **Defined Roles:** Assigns specific responsibilities, including the Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers.
- **Ceremonies:** Requires specific events like daily standups, sprint planning, and retrospectives.[[1]](https://slack.com/blog/collaboration/agile-vs-scrum)[[2]](https://projectmanagementacademy.net/resources/blog/agile-vs-scrum-what-you-need-to-know/)[[3]](https://miro.com/agile/scrum-vs-agile-methodology/)[[4]](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/scrum/agile-vs-scrum)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ls2F3y4kSFA&vl=en&t=95)

### Key Differences
| Feature | Agile | Scrum |
|---|---|---|
| **Type** | Philosophy and mindset | Actionable framework |
| **Rules** | Open-ended and adaptable | Prescriptive with strict rules |
| **Roles** | Not explicitly defined | Product Owner, Scrum Master, Team |
| **Workflow** | Continuous delivery or flow | Time-boxed Sprints |

If you'd like, let me know:

- What **kind of project or team** you are working with
- Whether you prefer **strict structure** or **continuous flow** 

I can help you decide if Scrum or another Agile approach fits best.
